A **backreference** lets you match the same text that was previously captured by a group in the regex pattern.

**Example:** `(\w+)\s+\1` matches a word repeated twice with whitespace between them.

- `(\w+)` captures one or more word characters into group 1
- `\s+` matches whitespace
- `\1` backreferences group 1, requiring it to match the exact same text

This pattern matches `"hello hello"` and `"the the"`, but not `"hello world"`. Backreferences are written as `\1`, `\2`, etc. (or `$1`, `$2` in replacement strings, depending on the language).
